paragraphs.title: The Conquest of Rabbah and the Land of Ammon

easy.explanation: The passage says that Joab led forth the army.
easy.q: Who led the army against the children of Ammon?
Where did David remain while Joab went to war?

easy.explanation: David took the king's crown from off his head.
easy.q: What did David take from the head of the king of Ammon?

answers: He took the crown and abundant spoil
He sent Joab back to Jerusalem
medium.explanation: David took the crown and brought exceeding much spoil out of the city.
medium.q: What did David do after Joab destroyed Rabbah?

medium.explanation: The word “weigh” refers to the crown's weight.
medium.q: In the phrase “it to weigh a talent of gold,” what does “weigh” mean?

answers: David treated the other Ammonite cities in the same way
David left every Ammonite city untouched
David gave the cities to Joab
medium.explanation: The statement extends David's actions to all the Ammonite cities.
medium.q: What does “Even so dealt David with all the cities of the children of Ammon” show?

answers: Joab stayed in Jerusalem while David fought
Joab led the campaign, while David received the crown and spoil
challenge.explanation: Joab led the army and destroyed Rabbah; David later took the crown and spoil.
challenge.q: What difference between Joab's and David's roles is shown in the passage?

answers: David gave the crown to Joab as a gift
The crown had been found in Jerusalem before the war
The crown was taken as a result of conquering the city
challenge.explanation: After Rabbah was destroyed, David took its king's crown.
challenge.q: What is the connection between the conquest of Rabbah and the crown being placed on David's head?

answers: A great amount of booty was taken from the city
All the city's inhabitants escaped safely
challenge.explanation: The phrase describes the large amount of spoil taken from Rabbah.
challenge.q: What does bringing “exceeding much spoil out of the city” indicate?

paragraphs.title: Israel's Victories over the Philistine Giants

easy.explanation: The passage mentions battles at Gezer and Gath.
easy.q: At which places did the battles with the Philistines take place?

easy.explanation: Jonathan the son of Shimea slew him.
easy.q: Who slew the man with twenty-four fingers and toes?

medium.explanation: The passage names Sibbechai first, then Elhanan, and finally Jonathan.
medium.q: In what order are the Israelite warriors mentioned as defeating the Philistines?

answers: The brother of Goliath the Gittite
medium.explanation: Elhanan slew Lahmi, the brother of Goliath the Gittite.
medium.q: Who was Lahmi according to the passage?

medium.explanation: The passage compares his spear staff to a weaver's beam.
medium.q: What was the spear staff of Lahmi like?

answers: There were several battles, not just one
All the battles happened on the same day
There were no further battles after the first one
challenge.explanation: The repeated wording shows that additional battles took place.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the repeated descriptions of another war with the Philistines?

answers: He had twenty-four fingers and toes
challenge.explanation: Six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot highlight his extraordinary size.
challenge.q: Which detail most strongly emphasizes the unusual size of the man from Gath?

answers: The descendants of the giant fell by the hand of David and his servants
challenge.explanation: The final verse says that these descendants of the giant fell by David and his servants.
challenge.q: What overall result of these battles is given at the end of the passage?
